                                                            for n, v in vals.items()]})

                    continue
                means = rows.groupby(segs[:2])[c].mean()
                top = ranked(rows.groupby(segs[:2]).size()).head(20).index
                raw["segments"].append({"segment_column": joint, "metric_column": c, "aggregation": "mean",
                                        "results": [{"name": f"{a}|{b}", "value": round(float(means[(a, b)]), 4)}
                                                    for a, b in top]})
                raw["builtin"].append(f"seg:{joint}/{c}")

expert_review.review_summary: 10 claims checked against the evidence; 1 flagged (1 unsupported).
gaps: The analysis does not examine tenure or time-to-exit patterns. Understanding how long employees stay before separating (by department or job level) would help identify whether high attrition reflects early-career departures or experienced-staff losses.

No breakdown of attrition by Employment Status or Termination Category is provided. Knowing whether Support's high exit rate (116.3%) reflects active terminations, resignations, or other categories would clarify the nature of the problem.

Performance Rating trends show declines (down 25% MoM, down 10.4% YoY overall), but no analysis connects performance to attrition or regrettable terminations. Examining whether low performers are more likely to separate would inform retention strategy.
next_investigations: Compare attrition and regrettable termination rates by Job Level within each high-attrition department (Support, Sales, Engineering) to identify whether exits concentrate at entry levels or senior roles.

Analyze the relationship between Performance Rating and Regrettable Termination by department to determine whether regrettable losses are high performers or whether performance ratings differ between regrettable and non-regrettable separations.
Examine tenure (months from Hire Date to Termination Date or current date) by department and job level to identify whether high attrition reflects early departures or loss of experienced staff.
methodology_concerns: Month-over-month trends for Annual Salary, Performance Rating, and Full Time Equivalent are computed on only 2–4 rows (Nov 2026 vs Oct 2026), yielding low confidence. These trends should not be used for decision-making without larger sample sizes or longer periods.

Annual Salary is missing for 7% of records (121 of 1,770 rows), and all salary-based analyses exclude these rows. Segmented means (by Department, Job Level) are computed on 1,649 rows; the missing data may not be random and could bias comparisons if missingness correlates with department or level.

Support's departmental attrition rate is reported as 116.3% (1.1627), which exceeds 100%. This occurs when separations in the 12-month period exceed the average headcount over that period, indicating high turnover relative to workforce size; the interpretation should clarify this is a rate, not a percentage of current staff.
